---
title: "Top of climb and top of descent"
description: "How OPDI finds the end of the climb to cruise (top-of-climb) and the start of the final descent (top-of-descent)."
---

## In one sentence

`top-of-climb` marks where the climb to cruise ends and `top-of-descent`
where the final descent starts, by the method of EUROCONTROL's vertical flight
efficiency indicators.

## What it needs

- The barometric altitude of the track after cleaning (see
  [Cleaning of position reports](cleaning.qmd)). Altitudes below −2,000 ft or
  above 60,000 ft, and altitudes of reports flagged on the ground, are not
  used: transponders on the ground sometimes send altitudes of 9,800 to
  126,000 ft.
- The departure and destination airports of the flight list, for the 200 NM
  circles around them. Without one of them, the start or end of the track is
  used instead.
- The level segments of the track (see [Level segments](level-segments.qmd#pru-level-segments)).

## How it is computed

1. **Analysis area.** For each report, compute the great-circle distance to
   the departure and destination airports. Find the first moment the aircraft
   is 200 NM or more from the departure airport (D200; the end of the track if
   it never is) and the last moment it is more than 200 NM from the
   destination airport (A200; the start of the track if it never is). A step
   climb further than 200 NM out is cruise, not climb.
2. **First estimate.** The top of climb is the first moment the aircraft
   reaches its highest altitude between the start of the track and D200. The
   top of descent is the last moment it is at its highest altitude between
   A200 and the end of the track. `info.d200_time` and `info.d200_altitude_ft`
   keep this estimate.
3. **Exclusion box.** The box runs from the estimated top's altitude down to
   90% of it. A level segment inside the box that lasts more than 300 s is
   cruise. If one starts before the estimated top of climb, the top of climb
   moves to the start of the first such segment, at its altitude; the top of
   descent likewise moves to the end of the last such segment after its
   estimate. `info.relocated` says whether the top moved.
4. **Position.** The top takes the position of the report with a position
   nearest in time to it, within 60 s; without one it has no position.
5. **Observed or at the edge of reception.** `info.observed` is true on a top
   of climb when the track has an altitude at least 3,000 ft lower before it,
   and on a top of descent when it has one at least 3,000 ft lower after it.
   Otherwise the top sits where reception starts or ends (a track first
   received in cruise) and `info.observed` is false.

Each track has at most one top of climb and one top of descent.

## Based on

The vertical flight efficiency method of the EUROCONTROL Performance Review
Unit (PRU): the 200 NM radius, the first and last points of highest
altitude, and the exclusion box at 90% of the top with 300 s. The position
rule (step 4) and `info.observed` (step 5) were added for OPDI. The study is
[Flight events from ADS-B, version 4](../../papers/flight-events-v4/index.html).

## What is published

Event types `top-of-climb` and `top-of-descent`, with position, altitude,
`distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds `d200_time`,
`d200_altitude_ft`, `relocated`, `analysis_radius_nm` (200), `method` (`pru`)
and `observed` (see the [Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Cruise altitude and its share of the flight**: the altitude of the tops,
  and the distance flown between them.
- **Vertical flight efficiency**: with the level-offs, the climb and descent
  profiles below the tops, per airport pair.
- **Descent planning**: the distance from `top-of-descent` to `ALDT`, from
  `distance_flown_nm`.

## Limitations

A flight without a real cruise (a short flight, a training flight) gets its
highest report as tops, and a track holding several flights gets only one
pair. Use `info.observed` to leave out tops at the edge of reception. See
[Limitations: vertical profile](../limitations.qmd#lim-vertical).
